prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can give good, actionable recommendations — but to point you to the best local contractors I should know your Atlanta ZIP code or neighborhood so I can recommend teams that actually serve your street and have nearby crews. If you want a quick starter list now, here are solid, reputable options that serve the Atlanta metro and why you should call them, plus how to choose between estimates.

Specific companies to contact (serve Atlanta metro)
- Coolray — Large regional HVAC company with many local crews, good online reviews, offers manufacturer-authorized installs, financing and routine maintenance plans. Good for fast scheduling and standard new-system installs.
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (and Mister Sparky/Benjamin Franklin franchises under the same parent) — National franchise with local Atlanta offices, widely available, often provides clear written guarantees and service windows.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (part of Neighborly) — Big national provider with local Atlanta teams, full-service (installation, ductwork, plumbing), often has strong emergency service options and financing.
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning — National brand with local Atlanta dealers; many technicians are manufacturer- and NATE-certified, they typically provide written estimates, system design and extended warranties.
- A local Carrier or Trane factory-authorized dealer — Use Carrier/Trane dealer locators (on their websites) to find dealers in Atlanta who are certified by the manufacturer — that usually means better warranty handling and proper equipment matching.

Why these are worth calling
- Manufacturer authorization and NATE-certified techs: better likelihood of properly sized installs and valid warranties.
- Financing/warranty options: these firms commonly offer 0% or low-interest financing and extended labor warranties.
- Volume + local presence: quicker scheduling, dedicated local crews, and more online reviews to vet them.
- Service breadth: they handle ductwork, permits, and disposal of old equipment — important for a complete replacement.

How to get the best install (what to ask and compare)
1. Get at least 3 written estimates (not ballparks). Ask for:
   - Manual J load calculation for proper sizing
   - Make/model and SEER rating of proposed equipment
   - Full scope: new condensers/air handlers/ductwork/thermostat, permit costs, disposal
   - Labor warranty and manufacturer warranty details, and whether the dealer registers the warranty
   - Financing options, incentives, rebates, and estimated running costs
2. Verify credentials:
   - Georgia contractor registration / local license and proof of insurance
   - NATE certification for technicians
   - Manufacturer dealer certification if they claim it
   - Check Google reviews, Angi, Yelp, and BBB for recent complaints
3. Compare apples-to-apples: same equipment or equivalent SEER and brand, same ductwork scope, same permit inclusion.
4. Ask about energy-efficiency and indoor-air options: high-SEER units, variable-speed compressors, zoning, and smart thermostats.
5. Timing and start-to-finish window — ask how long the install will take and when they can start.

Next step
If you give me your Atlanta ZIP code or neighborhood (e.g., Midtown, Buckhead, Decatur, East Point), I’ll:
- List 3–5 specific contractors near you with known service areas and recent review summaries
- Highlight which ones are factory-authorized dealers for Carrier/Trane/Trane etc.
- Suggest which two to get estimates from first based on your priorities (lowest price, best warranty, best reviews).

Which neighborhood or ZIP code should I use?
